title: The Second Site
space: the student's own vhost directory `/srv/webroot/{user}/` and names under `{user}.certs.dojo.test`
goal: Give `shop.{user}.certs.dojo.test` its own trusted certificate, using either tool, without touching the first site.
verify_text: `demo-app`'s HTTPS listener serves `shop.{user}.certs.dojo.test` (checked over SNI) a certificate that chains to the CA root, matches the name and is not expired, and is not the certificate served for `{user}.certs.dojo.test`. It cannot see whether the first site's serial changed, only that the two sites hold different certificates. And `shop.conf` on `main` of `{user}/cert-shop` names `shop.{user}.certs.dojo.test` and has a `listen 443 ssl` block (push the vhost you run). The repo's whole history (every branch, every commit) holds no private key.
isolation: a second vhost in the student's own subdirectory and the student's own repo `{user}/cert-shop`; issuance goes through the shared CA, which handles concurrent orders for different names. The check reads only names under `{user}.certs.dojo.test` and that repo.
hints: Same steps as your first site, new hostname.
New vhost, new issuance, new install.
seed: `dojo-challenge start c1` creates `{user}/cert-shop` (owned by the student, cloned to `~/lab/cert-shop`): a brief and `shop.conf`, a port-80 vhost for `shop.{user}.certs.dojo.test` with its own webroot folder. The wildcard A record `*.{user}.certs.dojo.test` (made for every student by the DNS seed at stack start, pointing at `demo-app`) is what makes the name resolve.
answer: `dojo-challenge start c1`, copy `shop.conf` into `/srv/webroot/{user}/conf.d/` and make `shop-html`, issue for `shop.{user}.certs.dojo.test` with certbot (Lab 2) or acme.sh (Lab 3) into a folder of its own, add a `listen 443 ssl` block pointing at that certificate, copy it in again, push `shop.conf` to `main` (no key in the repo), and run `dojo-check c1`.
